OnPlay.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): The verb is ported, once, and both callers now use it: `CardPileCmd.auto_play_from_draw_pile` (sts2_rl/cmds.py) is CardPileCmd.AutoPlayFromDrawPile (CardPileCmd.cs:931-966) with BOTH phases. Phase 1 (:939-955) pulls all `count` picks out of the draw pile into PileType.Play -- one ShuffleIfNecessary per pick (:939), `break` not `continue` on an empty pile (:949-952) -- and phase 2 (:956-965) plays them, setting `ExhaustOnNextPlay = forceExhaust` on each (:960) and breaking if the owner has died (:958). So every pick is COMMITTED before any of them resolves, and because the waiting cards sit in PileType.Play a reshuffle the first one triggers excludes them (bug class 7). `force_exhaust` goes through `exhaust_on_next_play` rather than a hand-move, which is what routes an UNPLAYABLE pick to CardCmd.Exhaust (CardModel.cs:2098-2101) and still lets a Power card vanish to PileType.None (:2071-2074). Supporting ports, both cited in place: `PlayerCombatState.shuffle_if_necessary` (CardPileCmd.cs:972-981) and `CombatState._move_to_result_pile_without_playing` (CardModel.cs:2089-2107, which the sim had as a bare `discard_pile.append`).  This site: Havoc.cs:21 is that one call with count 1, Top, forceExhaust true, and cards/havoc.py is now that one call. The bracket the hand-rolled version skipped is all back, because the play goes through `_resolve_card_play`: the per-play-index BeforeCardPlayed/AfterCardPlayed pair, `on_energy_spent(card, 0)` (Free Attack), the play-count loop seeded from `1 + base_replay_count`, the before_attack/after_attack bracket (Akabeko's Vigor), the in-loop EnchantmentModel.OnPlay call, and `captured_x` for X-cost cards. EXECUTED: a Hidden-Gem'd Strike off the draw pile now deals 6 TWICE; the played card is exhausted through the result-pile path; an unplayable Burn is EXHAUSTED rather than discarded; a Power card vanishes and still grants its power. It also drops two further hand-rolled defects -- an UNSTABLE inline reshuffle where ShuffleIfNecessary is a StableShuffle, and a `not is_gone` target roll where CardCmd.cs:77 is `Rng.CombatTargets.NextItem(HittableEnemies)` (fixed in `auto_play_card`, the Batch-1 mechanism's last unrouted site). ONE ENGINE CHANGE CAME WITH IT, and it is recorded because it is a legacy-behaviour change: the PileType.Play hold-back in `reshuffle_discard_into_draw` / `shuffle_draw_and_discard` (sts2_rl/player.py) was gated on `combat_rng.is_parity`, so in legacy mode a card mid-OnPlay WAS reshuffled out of the discard. With the real verb that is an infinite recursion (Havoc is handed back to the draw pile and picked as the top card again), and it was never a defensible second side -- the game holds the card in limbo in both modes. The gate is gone. MEASURED before removing it: the full suite passes either way apart from the six tests this round moved for unrelated reasons. Pinned by test/test_auto_play_from_draw_pile.py (11 tests) and the pre-existing test_ironclad_cards.py::TestHavoc::test_no_crash_with_empty_piles, which is the recursion witness. C#'s `CardPileCmd.AutoPlayFromDrawPile` reaches `OnPlayWrapper` and runs the full bracket (Havoc.cs:21 -> CardCmd.cs:129). The bracket half got LARGER, not smaller, in the fix campaign: `_resolve_card_play` now runs BeforeCardPlayed and AfterCardPlayed once per play index rather than once per logical play, so Havoc drops more per auto-play than it did when this entry was written. LIVE: Havoc is a ported Common and Akabeko, Hidden Gem, the Spiral enchantment and X-cost cards are all ported. The fix shape is unchanged -- pull the card off the draw pile, then call `ctx.combat.auto_play_card(card)`, as card/cascade does. HISTORY -- WHAT THE DIVERGENCE WAS: C# is a single line: `CardPileCmd.AutoPlayFromDrawPile(choiceContext, Owner, 1, CardPilePosition.Top, forceExhaust: true)` (Havoc.cs:21). The sim reimplements the whole verb inline AND, unlike card/cascade -- which reimplements the same verb faithfully -- it does not route the play through `CombatState.auto_play_card`. It calls `card.on_play(ctx, idx)` directly (havoc.py:52, 57), which SKIPS the entire play bracket that `_resolve_card_play` provides (combat.py:441-513): `hooks.on_energy_spent(card, 0)` (so Free Attack and any other BeforeCardPlayed listener never fires -- C#'s AutoPlay reaches `OnPlayWrapper` and runs the full bracket, CardCmd.cs:129), `hooks.before_card_played`, the play-count loop from `modify_card_play_count` (so a Spiral-enchanted or Hidden-Gem'd card plays ONCE instead of twice), the `before_attack`/`after_attack` bracket (so Vigor from Akabeko is not consumed), and `captured_x` for X-cost cards (so a Whirlwind auto-played by Havoc does nothing). It also picks the random target with `ctx.combat._rng.choice(living)` (havoc.py:56) -- the unseeded shared rng -- where `auto_play_card` correctly uses `self.combat_rng.targets` with the CardCmd.cs:77 citation in-line (combat.py:540-546), so Havoc is also one of the 21 cards the `shared-rng` probe lists. LIVE on every count: Havoc is a ported Common, and Akabeko, Hidden Gem, the Spiral enchantment and X-cost cards are all ported. The fix shape is the one card/cascade already uses -- pull the card off the draw pile, then call `ctx.combat.auto_play_card(card)`. Presentation: none in the C# body. REGRESSION TEST: `test/test_rng_tripwire.py:33` (`test_no_wrong_stream_draws_in_random_run`, 20 seeded full runs) is the standing gate for this whole family. It wraps `RunState.rng` and asserts ZERO in-combat draws on it; `CombatState` receives that same object as `self._rng` (run.py:1146-1148, combat.py:88), so a `ctx.combat._rng` draw taken from inside a card's `on_play` is recorded and fails the gate -- verified by playing this family's shape under a `Tripwire` and getting a hit at the `card.on_play` frame (combat.py:490). The gate is green today, so these 20 seeds never reach this card's draw; routing the site to the named `combat_rng` accessor is verified by keeping it green.

guards.rationale: Faithful to `AutoPlayFromDrawPile`'s per-iteration `ShuffleIfNecessary` (CardPileCmd.cs:941) and its `FirstOrDefault()` top-of-pile pick (945): the sim reshuffles only when the draw pile is empty and the discard is not, uses the named `combat_rng.shuffle` stream, fires `on_shuffle`, and pops the END of its draw pile, which is its top. Returning early when both piles are empty matches C#'s `cardModel == null` break (949-952).

guards.issue: C# sets `item.ExhaustOnNextPlay = forceExhaust` (CardPileCmd.cs:960) and lets the play pipeline route the card to the exhaust pile, which means the card passes through PileType.Play first and lands in Exhaust through `CardPileCmd.Add`. The sim appends straight to `exhaust_pile` and fires `on_card_exhausted`, skipping the result-pile redirect hook (`modify_card_play_result_pile`, combat.py:505-509 -- Nostalgia) that C# would consult. DORMANT: Nostalgia redirects Attack/Skill plays to the top of the DRAW pile, and C#'s ExhaustOnNextPlay takes precedence over the result-pile choice, so the two agree today; live if a ported result-pile modifier ever outranks a forced exhaust. Recorded separately from the OnPlay entry because it is a distinct mechanism.
